x: In the Huddersfield Road Runners 10km event on February 23rd, Steve Halliday, the 23 year old former Yorkshire Champion, won his first race in over a year wearing the colours of his new club Belgrave for the first time.

Steve Halliday is beginning to look good in the 1500 while Lewis Samuel was still not happy with his pace judgement in the 400 metres. Nevertheless the long relay squad achieved a notable second and the late surge replenished spirits for the coach journey home, which for some finished at 5 am Sunday morning!
Steve Halliday made a steady debut for us in the 'A' 1500 metres while Stuart Paton seemed to be in a race designed for his kick finish but it was not to be.
A week after running the 'A' 1500 in BAL match 1 at Birmingham Steve Halliday was back on the roads for the Halifax Courier 10k. He won it by a minute and a half in 30:53.
Steve Halliday tussled for the lead early on but had to give way finally to Valli's Paul Cuskin, who relieved our man of his course record by clocking 30:36, and Skyrac's Peter Whitehead.

…high mileage marathon training: "Can't I run two legs ?" Then a half fit Frank Ward got round on memory to hand over to Steve Halliday, down from Halifax for the race, as cheery as ever and having a blinding run with 4th fastest long stage of the day to move Belgrave up from 17th to 10th.…

Stage 1 was taken by Steve Halliday who was most certainly on for one of the fastest times of the day - except that while holding a 70 yard lead over the field he went off course, lost about a minute, and then trailed in a disconsolate 18th!
Grand Prix 10k. 6, M.Lake 32:31; 8, M.Webb 32:36. Almondbury 10k, 18 Aug. 2, S.Halliday 32:27. Burnsall, 21 Aug. 10miles. 1, S.Halliday 52:16.

Second place would have been good points but a very doubtful measuring of the Hungarian competitor's fourth throw by officials from his own club suddenly had our big man in 3rd. Steve Halliday was delighted with his 1500m. The last lap was ferocious but our Yorkshireman was not found wanting.
Steve Halliday led early on in the 5000m but was caught by Bradford Airdale's Richard Findlow to lose out 14:57.9 to 14:50.34.

Elsewhere Steve Halliday and Rob Turner produced excellent 1500m times while Darrell Maynard suffered niggling injuries and never realised his potential (although he did gain a Welsh vest) and Dave Scott made a welcome return from his year's globetrotting.
R.Turner 3:49.67; S.Halliday 3:50.38. 3000m: 14, R.Alsop 8:39.37. 10000m: 1, P.Evans 28:17.49; G.Staines dnf. 110m: 3, N.Owen 14.03. 400mH: hts.
Neil Owen continued his winning ways in the sprint hurdles while Steve Halliday, fresh from his good performance in Budapest, scored maximum points in both the 'B' 800 and the 'A' 1500.
Marcello pulled a calf muscle in the 5000m and a sick Steve Halliday doubled up in the 1500 and 5000m but it all proved too much and we drifted to 3rd but retained overall 2nd place in the league.
